articles.headline: OFAC Announces Settlement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics, Designates International Criminal Court, and Removes Burma-Related Designation
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Pegasus Worldwide Logistics on October 9, 2026. Concurrently, OFAC designated the International Criminal Court and issued related General Licenses.
In a separate action, OFAC also announced the removal of a Burma-related designation, indicating a shift in sanctions policy concerning certain entities or individuals associated with Burma.
These actions reflect OFAC's ongoing efforts to enforce sanctions, adapt to geopolitical developments, and refine its lists of sanctioned entities and individuals.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues New Russia-Related General License
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued a new Russia-related General License on October 9, 2026.
This new General License provides specific authorizations for certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited under existing Russia sanctions programs.

The issuance of General Licenses often indicates a refinement of sanctions policy to allow for particular activities deemed permissible or necessary for humanitarian, economic, or other policy reasons.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-Related Designations, Issues New Iran and Amended Russia General Licenses
body: On October 8, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations, expanding the scope of sanctions targeting entities and individuals connected to Iran.

In conjunction with these designations, OFAC also issued a new Iran-related General License, which may permit certain transactions that would otherwise be prohibited. Additionally, an amended Russia-related General License was issued, indicating adjustments to existing authorizations concerning Russia.
These actions underscore the U.S. government's continued focus on applying pressure on Iran while also making calibrated adjustments to sanctions regimes related to both Iran and Russia.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Designations Removals and Updates, Publishes Iran-Related Alert and Amended FAQ
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced several designations removals and updates on October 5, 2026, indicating a review and adjustment of its sanctions lists.

Furthermore, OFAC published an Iran-related Alert, warning foreign financial institutions that they could be targeted without advance notification if they continue to transact with sanctioned Iranian financial institutions.

An amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question (FAQ) was also published, clarifying aspects of the Iran sanctions program and removing language that previously indicated OFAC would generally contact foreign financial institutions before making a finding of sanctionable activity.
articles.source: U.S. Treasury OFAC / Global Sanctions and Export Controls Blog

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Terrorism Designations
body: On October 2, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Counter Terrorism Designations.
These designations target individuals and entities identified as supporting terrorist organizations or activities, aiming to disrupt their financial networks and operations.
The action reinforces the U.S. government's commitment to combating global terrorism through financial sanctions.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Iran-Related Designations and Updates, Targets Transnational Criminal Organizations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and designations updates on October 1, 2026, further tightening sanctions against the Iranian regime.
Additionally, OFAC designated entities involved in Transnational Criminal Organizations, highlighting the intersection of illicit finance and national security concerns.
The Treasury Department also published an Iran-related Determination and an amended Iran-related Frequently Asked Question, providing further guidance and clarity on the scope of the sanctions.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organizations, Removes Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya Designations
body: On September 30, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting Counter Terrorism and Transnational Criminal Organizations.
In a separate move, OFAC also announced the removal of several designations related to Belarus, Counter Narcotics, and Libya, indicating a recalibration of sanctions in these areas.
These actions demonstrate OFAC's dynamic approach to sanctions, adding new targets while also delisting others based on evolving policy considerations.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes New Counter Narcotics, Counter Terrorism, Iran-Related, and Non-Proliferation Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a broad set of new designations on September 29, 2026, targeting entities and individuals involved in Counter Narcotics, Counter Terrorism, Iran-related activities, and Non-Proliferation.
These comprehensive designations underscore the U.S. government's multi-faceted approach to combating various threats to national security and foreign policy.
The actions aim to disrupt illicit networks and prevent the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, as well as to counter terrorism and narcotics trafficking.

articles.headline: OFAC Publishes Regulatory Amendments, Cuba Sanctions Regulations, and New FAQs
body: On September 29, 2026, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced the publication of regulatory amendments and new Cuba Sanctions Regulations.
This update includes the issuance of new and amended Cuba-related Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs), providing further guidance on the scope and application of the sanctions program.
Additionally, OFAC published a Cuba-related Alert, signaling continued vigilance and enforcement in relation to transactions involving Cuba.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Venezuela General Licenses
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued amended Venezuela General Licenses on September 28, 2026.
These amendments modify existing authorizations for certain transactions related to Venezuela, reflecting ongoing adjustments to U.S. policy towards the country.
General Licenses are frequently updated to respond to evolving political and economic conditions, allowing for specific activities while maintaining overall sanctions pressure.

articles.headline: OCC Issues Cease-and-Desist Order and $350 Million Penalty Against American Express National Bank for BSA/AML Failures
body: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) announced a cease-and-desist order and a $350 million civil money penalty against American Express National Bank, Sandy, Utah.
The enforcement action stems from significant deficiencies in the bank's Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) and anti-money laundering (AML) compliance program.

The OCC found that the bank failed to establish and maintain a BSA/AML compliance program reasonably designed to assure and monitor compliance with the BSA and its implementing regulations, including inadequate resources, systemic internal control gaps, weak independent testing, and insufficient training.

articles.headline: FinCEN Assesses Record $125 Million Penalty Against UBS Financial Services Inc. for Recidivist BSA Violations
body: The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) assessed a historic $125 million civil money penalty against UBS Financial Services Inc. (UBSFS) for willful and recidivist violations of the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA).
This is the largest penalty ever imposed against a broker-dealer for BSA violations to date.

FinCEN found that UBSFS failed to address underlying problems identified in a 2018 consent order, including inadequate monitoring of foreign currency wires and deficient customer due diligence for high-risk customers with ties to Russia and Latin America.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
